cells.tense: You are here, holding more feeling than one situation should hold, and you have not dropped any of it.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: This week, take the heaviest load on you and put its real cost in numbers — hours, sleep, what gets skipped. Read what comes out, and keep the page somewhere it'll catch your eye.
cells.core:
You can stand under a heavy week and still feel all of it. A room turns when someone walks in and you notice. An old want sits beside a new one and neither knocks you over. That isn't being unsteady. You take feeling in without letting it decide for you, and the weight gets carried while you stand there.

There's arithmetic hidden in what you carry. Choose the heaviest thing on you and put its real cost into numbers — hours, sleep, whatever gets skipped. Read what comes out. What you'll see is whether the weight belongs to the situation or to your grip on it. One count, read once, kept where it catches your eye.

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future that keeps arriving heavier than you can hold it down.
cells.act: protect what was won by the ending
cells.ask: Bring a thing you're hauling toward an unfixed future to a finish — written, said, handed over — and put it somewhere it stays done. Then set your hands down.
cells.core:
When the load settles on you, you've started bracing before it lands. Every version of how things might end gets gathered ahead of time — every feeling that could still arrive — and none gets put down. Bearing weight under that turns into hanging on until the future reports back. You can carry a lot. Carrying all of it before it exists is what makes it too heavy.

One of those can close. Bring a thing you're hauling toward a future that isn't here to an end you can point to — written, said, handed over — and put it somewhere it stays done. What it already earned stands without your grip. The turns after come one at a time, and one at a time you carry them fine.
cells.sheetLine: Holding what hasn't happened is what's breaking your grip.

cells.tense: The door opens more times than you go through it, and you are still standing where it used to be.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Give an hour to nothing that needs solving — a walk with no route, a chair with no plan. When a problem surfaces, don't reach for it. Let it sit there.
cells.core:
Near the weight, you've gone quiet. Endurance flattens into standing still — you take what comes, answer little, and don't reach for what someone might feel or want from you. Nothing has broken. Fewer things move toward you than they could, and what you do feel gets said after it's too late to say it.

Relief won't come from carrying more. Give the part of you that keeps working the problem an hour off — a walk with no route, a chair with no plan. Anything that comes up while you're in it, let it sit. Once you've stopped working it, you can look at one open thing and see it as it is. The hour comes first.

cells.tense: The choice gets made on time, arrives in you already done, and your name is not on it.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: Next time something lands heavy, drop the story and trace the one consequence that follows from it. Let that be why you move, and call it yours.
cells.core:
You read what a heavy week holds before most people see it — which person matters, which want is real, what can be answered and what should wait. That reading keeps happening, and you'd call it just getting through. The deciding is yours. It shows up filed under circumstances.

When something lands heavy again, walk past the story to the one consequence that follows from it. Not the reaction around it, not anyone's agreement — the thing that comes after. Let that be why you move. The call was yours the whole time. This lets you watch your own hand make it, and keep it.

attempts.check: Unsupported: that a person carrying Fortitude actually gathers emotional possibilities the way the draw says — the seat does not prove the mechanism, and the core names the pulling without claiming it is happening now. A reader could say the too-little cell locates a door behind them, which the record doesn't state; it is narrowed to what someone could do — look again at one option — so it stands even if the behind-the-door read is wrong. The ask survives a wrong read either way: watering one, deciding one, resting an hour, counting an option's costs all remain useful undoings. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line about the weight of feeling being held; it's cut. The card holds its name, the seat its place; the asks are the four medicines' own listed acts.
